svg.title: The eight Layer 2 defenses as one matrix: what each stops, where it is applied and the design gotcha that makes it fail
svg.desc: Eight rows. BPDU Guard, Root Guard and Loop Guard stop root takeover and BPDU flooding and are applied to edge or downstream ports, with the gotcha that BPDU Guard err-disables the port while Root Guard only puts it in root-inconsistent and recovers by itself. Disabling DTP and moving the native VLAN to an unused VLAN stops VLAN hopping and belongs on every access port and trunk, with the gotcha that the native VLAN must carry no service and have no SVI. Port security stops MAC flooding and CAM overflow on access ports, but the sticky table and the MAB whitelist must be maintained by the same system. Dynamic ARP inspection stops ARP spoofing and depends entirely on the DHCP snooping binding table. DHCP snooping and IP Source Guard stop rogue DHCP servers and source address spoofing, but static hosts need static bindings. IPv6 RA Guard stops rogue router advertisements and is the one everyone forgets because IPv6 is unmanaged. 802.1X with MAB is the only control that moves admission from the physical layer to identity, and the gotchas are method choice, host mode and the fallback when RADIUS is down. Private VLAN and MACsec cover lateral movement inside a VLAN and link eavesdropping respectively, at the cost of configuration complexity and about thirty-two bytes of MTU. A footer lists the four cheapest controls.
svg.text: Eight Layer 2 controls on one page: what each buys, where it goes, and how it fails
Read the fourth column first - almost every "we enabled it" incident is a gotcha from that column, not a missing command
THE GOTCHA THAT MAKES IT USELESS
BPDU Guard err-disables and needs a human to recover;
Root Guard only becomes root-inconsistent and self-heals
The native VLAN must carry no traffic at all: no SVI, no
access port. Otherwise a successful hop lands in live VLAN
overflow, which turns the VLAN into a hub
The sticky table becomes a second MAC whitelist. If MAB
exists too, both must be generated from the same source
man in the middle that follows it
It checks ARP against the DHCP snooping binding table, so
an empty table means either everything passes or everything drops
address spoofing on the access port
Static hosts are dropped until a static binding exists -
printers and building controllers are the usual casualties
that silently become the default gateway
The forgotten control: teams say "we are not running IPv6"
while every Windows host has a link-local address and listens
the port - the only identity-based control
MAB for devices without a supplicant
Three decisions decide success: method (EAP-TLS vs PEAP vs
MAB), host mode, and the fallback when RADIUS is unreachable
PVLAN in one L2 domain, MACsec on
PVLAN does not exist inside VXLAN/EVPN; MACsec adds ~32
bytes, so MTU and both ends' hardware must be checked first
The four that cost almost nothing:
shut unused ports · nonegotiate + native VLAN 999 · BPDU Guard on every edge port · DHCP snooping on every access port. Do these before designing anything clever.
